summary: Jens Augspurger works in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London by 2026, held a post at SOAS in 2018, lectured at IU International University (2022–2026), and joined the University of Mannheim in 2026.

Jens Braarvig is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a professorship at the University of Oslo in 2003 and is attested as a professor at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology in 2004.

Jens Peter Laut specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008, serving at the University of Göttingen (~2008–2021) and on the Leitungskommission of the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2008).

Jens Schlieter specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Vienna and Bonn (PhD ~1999 under Josef Simon). He worked at Bonn, Munich, and Bayreuth, becoming professor and institute director at the University of Bern around 2006.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned degrees from the University of Munich and completed his Habilitation at Göttingen. He was a professor at Berlin institutions and held a professorship at the University of Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London, completing her PhD in 2011 under doctoral supervisor Youngsook Pak and teacher Rosemary Smith.

Jerome Silbergeld is a scholar of Chinese art history and sinology who earned degrees at Stanford and Oregon. He served as department chair and director at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and as professor at Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jervoise Athelstane Baines was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rugby School, Trinity College, Cambridge (~1865–1868), and Trinity College Dublin. In 1901, he served as a Governor of the London School of Economics.

Jerzy Bańczerowski was a linguist who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961). He became head of its Department of General and Comparative Linguistics in 1969, served as professor (1977–1991), and was a member of the Polish Academy of Sciences.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Vienna, Lviv (PhD 1923), and under Antoine Meillet, Joseph Vendryes, and Theodor Bloch. He held professorships at the University of Lviv (1926–1946), Breslau (1946–1948), and Jagiellonian University (1948–1965).
Jessica Patey is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She is a PhD candidate studying and holding a post at Harvard University, attested in 2026.

Jessica X. Zu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed PhDs at Pennsylvania State University (1997–2003) and Princeton University (2013–2020), and became an associate professor at the University of Southern California in 2026.

Jessie Pons is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS, École du Louvre, Panthéon-Sorbonne, Sorbonne Nouvelle, and Sorbonne University (Doctorat 2011). At Ruhr University Bochum, she served as postdoctoral researcher, junior professor, and professor (2025).
Jesung Woo works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and held a post at Dongguk University, attested between 2001 and 2003.
Jey Flick works in Indology and Buddhist studies. Flick studied under Sheldon Pollock (attested 1984–2007) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley.
Jian Deng works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Deng was a disciple of Weijue Shi and succeeded Weijue Shi in 2005.
Jian Ouyang was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Renshan Yang (~1907–1911). He founded the China Institute of Inner Learning and served as its head from ~1922 to 1943.

Jiang Wu specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Nankai and Harvard, completing his dissertation under supervisors Tu Weiming and Robert M. Gimello by 2002. He served as a professor at the University of Arizona (attested 2011–2018).
Jianming Hu is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Hu studied at Waseda University (attested 2015) and held a post as a researcher at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Jiaqi Wang (1895–1959) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. Wang was a disciple of Gongga Rinpoche and is attested as a PhD student at Columbia University in 2026.
